items.title: Concord
items.note: A Sheffield dectet on Dwell Records playing five slow, improvised pieces with no drums and no voice. A Closer Listen says the players respond to tiny changes in each other's playing, and the shifts creep up on you over time.

items.title: One Of Many
items.note: The second album from an Amsterdam musician who composed, played and recorded all of it at home. It's self-released and tagged everywhere from Afro-Caribbean ritual music to drone and experimental jazz. That's exactly the kind of record an algorithm won't hand you.

items.title: Symbol Of The Land
items.note: Eleven tracks on the small Kynant label. Hard Wax calls it a warm, laid back, atmospheric dub electronic journey.

items.title: Toy (feat. Xenia Manasseh, tg.blk)
items.note: A soul single built around the back and forth between Xenia Manasseh and tg.blk. OkayAfrica calls it pure, unfiltered soul.

items.title: Bjerge, Strand
items.note: Bro's guitar with Larry Grenadier and Jorge Rossy, plus Charles Lloyd on saxophone and flute. JazzTrail calls it intimate and atmospheric, and picks out "Osaka" and "Peace Song" as favourites.

items.title: La Ola Nocturna: Experimental Songs and Deviant Pop from the Spanish 80's
items.note: Bongo Joe digs into post-punk, synthwave and darkwave from independent scenes across Spain after Franco, well beyond the usual Madrid Movida story. Bandcamp says it has something for both longtime fans and newcomers, with real oddities alongside the songs.

items.title: Wormhole Mystic
items.note: Minimal, rhythmic music built from synths, flute, saxophone and voice. It sits right where your beat and jazz sides meet.

items.title: Do Your Thing (A COLORS SHOW)
items.note: Her COLORS debut. OkayAfrica hears current British soul with a nostalgic swing, and it's a song about love.

items.title: Death/Rebirth One
items.note: Justin Broadrick's JK Flesh with the Canadian duo Orphx on KR3. Hard Wax sums it up as dark, heavy, raw techno, for when you want something with weight.

items.title: Forest of Tranquility
items.note: Seven long pieces on Erased Tapes in the Japanese environmental music tradition, each one shifting with the time of day. The press notes stress silence and point to Laraaji and Harold Budd. It's a quiet one to end on.

items.title: Wormhole Mystic
items.note: Twelve tracks built on old 60s and 70s drum machine loops, with Tenor adding synths, flute, sax and his own voice. Bureau B mentions Suicide and No Wave grooves, and calls one track cosmic drift.

items.artist: Anna Butterss, John Raymond, Ben Lumsdaine
items.title: Beginningless
items.note: Bass, trumpet and drums, fully improvised over two days in an LA studio with very little overdubbing. The Line of Best Fit gave it 8/10 for its open space and slow, hypnotic build.
items.source: Juno Jazz (found via The Line of Best Fit)

items.title: A New Day
items.note: Title track from the Dublin DJ and collector's new EP on Ascension On Wax, a small label that presses short vinyl runs. Dirty Disco played it in their deep, soulful house show this month.
items.source: Juno Deep House (found via Dirty Disco)

items.title: Heartbreak Stew
items.note: A debut from Copenhagen that puts acoustic guitar next to hyperpop and trap touches. Bandcamp Daily found it more cohesive than that mix suggests, with tender processed vocals.
items.source: Juno Leftfield (found via Bandcamp Daily Essential Releases)

items.title: Forest of Tranquility
items.note: The vibraphone player's new Erased Tapes album grew out of music he made for a living forest installation at Expo 2025. Seven long pieces that shift with the time of day.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (found via The Line of Best Fit)

items.title: EXPERTISE
items.note: Donwill's first proper album in seven years, over old-school boom bap and jazzy samples. Bandcamp Daily heard it as a joyful record that invites you to a party.
items.source: Juno Broken Beat / Nu-Jazz (found via Bandcamp Daily Album of the Day)

items.title: Whole Wide World
items.note: Title track from a two-year collaboration that grew out of touring together. Silent Radio describes the album as trance, distortion and experimental electronics with two live drummers.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (found via Silent Radio)

items.title: Traces in the Sand
items.note: His 27th solo album for ECM, dedicated to the sea and played on lamellophones he collected from places like Borneo, Japan and Armenia. It's about how the sea makes you feel, not a picture of it.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (found via uDiscover Music)

items.title: Cocon
items.note: Eight cellos with imagined electronic echoes, from a live audiovisual show with commissioned pieces including one by Sarah Davachi. Worth it if you like slow, physical string drone.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (found via Silent Radio)

items.title: ARP
items.note: A new modern classical record about pain, perseverance and family. We only read a short line on this one, so treat it as a tip to try.
items.source: Juno Ambient / Drone / Experimental (found via Silent Radio)

items.title: Saints in the Wethouse
items.note: The Lancashire artist's debut album, out Nov 13 on XL. Pitchfork hears heavy noise-rap with overwhelming bass, and the review's headline points to a turn from harsh noise toward ambient tenderness.

items.title: Love's Arp
items.note: His fourth album, out Nov 6 on True Panther. Pitchfork calls it muted experimental R&B, a tribute to a romance and to Black music history. Clash mentions East African rhythms, vintage gospel and house-inspired sound design.

items.title: Advanced White Trash
items.note: The LA saxophonist steps away from jazz here. Pitchfork describes Auto-Tuned vocals, hip-hop beats and fantasy themes, so expect something odd.

items.title: Music for Empty Stadiums
items.note: John Talabot's first solo full-length in over a decade, 95 minutes long on AD 93. He started it in lockdown, and Philip Sherburne's review hears dancefloor tracks built on sharp supersaws and cycling arpeggios.

items.title: SWALLOW!
items.note: Pitchfork 7.2. Her second album leans on trip-hop and big beat, and the review says the bonkers electronics are the best bits.

items.title: Texture Songs
items.note: Solo guitar and voice on Bill Orcutt's Palilalia label. Pitchfork notes extended guitar techniques and free-improv energy under quiet, understated singing.

items.title: Rapid Response EP
items.note: A 12-inch of three long pieces. Pitchfork hears him going further into dark new age psychedelia.

items.title: valley and structure
items.note: Pitchfork 7.4, the best score in this batch. A Thrill Jockey album that follows sentence structure in the country, the record Pitchfork says started a new stage for Rubio.

items.title: Quiet Forest
items.note: A reissue of his 1996 album, the last full-length released in his lifetime, inspired by a visit to the Hoh Rainforest. Pitchfork says it shows a playful side, and the new CD came out Nov 13 with vinyl due in December.

items.title: RUIN: It's Not Just Music
items.note: Pitchfork 6.4, so a mixed review that compares it with out-there records like Gush and The Kid. It is the first release on her own label, Someone Special.

items.title: Visual Culture of Northeast Brazil (Cordel Edition)
items.note: A 700-page study of cordel, the cheap pamphlet poetry of Brazil's Northeast with its woodcut covers. Victor Yves treats it as a communication system rather than folklore, with essays, close visual analysis, interviews and an anthology of more than 500 illustrations. It grew out of his CASCA Archive of Northeast Brazilian design, and comes as a small, thick, thread-sewn hardcover. Draw Down has it in stock too.

items.title: The Century of the Poster: Slovenian Poster Design in the 20th Century
items.note: More than 300 Slovenian posters, drawn from the visual communications collection at the Museum of Architecture and Design in Ljubljana and from libraries, archives and private holdings. It runs from early 20th century lithographs through modernism to post-socialist work, and reads the poster as a tool that shaped public space and political debate. 390 pages, paperback, in English. This week's poster book.

items.title: MXTP Vol. 2 (Music Typefaces)
items.note: The second font mixtape from Maxitype, the independent Swiss foundry and publisher. The typefaces came out of a summer type residency, and all of them are made for or inspired by music, from grunge and jungle to classical and Goa trance. 176 pages, hardcover, with a download code for 46 typefaces, so it is half specimen and half font library.

items.title: Bilingual Typography: A Guide to Categorisation and Design Principles
items.note: A small guide to setting two languages in one layout, built on Khajeh's doctoral research into Arabic and Latin typography and her own bilingual design work. It defines key terms, proposes new categories for bilingual layouts and sets out principles for balancing them. 144 pages, hardcover with a round spine, spot colours on uncoated paper. Ships in January 2027.

items.title: Design Subject to Change: Human Agency in the Digital Interface
items.note: Part manifesto and part confession from an interface designer who has spent a decade building software at scale. Spradlin asks why so many digital products now work against the people using them, drawing on design history, social theory and philosophy, and argues that the future of the interface is still open. Edited by Jarrett Fuller, with a foreword by Silvio Lorusso and a cover by Oliver Munday. 280 pages, expected mid to late January 2027.

items.title: The World's Best Typography: Typography 47
items.note: The latest Type Directors Club winners in communication design, lettering and typeface design, now published by Slanted. This edition is smaller and cheaper than before, with a Judges' Choices section where jurors explain their picks and an index of typefaces and designers. 384 pages, edited by Griffin McCabe and Joe Newton, art directed by Lars Harmsen and Marian Misiak.

items.title: The Best Dutch Book Designs 2025
items.note: The yearly round-up of the best designed Dutch books, presented by the Stedelijk Museum Amsterdam. Two juries pick the books, one of design, publishing and production people and one of graphic design students, and they look at typography, image editing, paper, printing and binding. 332 pages, Dutch and English. A good catalogue to steal ideas from.

items.title: To Have an Idea: 50 Years of Idea Books
items.note: Idea Books has distributed art, architecture and design books out of Amsterdam since 1976, and this is its 50th birthday book. Current and former staff, reps, publishers and customers share stories, next to archive documents, behind-the-scenes material and favourite titles. 156 pages, designed by Dongyoung Lee with photographs by Johannes Schwartz. A look at the part of the book world readers rarely see.

items.title: Mikhail Lychkovskiy
items.note: Poster designer who builds his work on type and grids, with Müller-Brockmann, Ruder and Hofmann as touchstones and French posters as a newer interest. He mostly works in Figma but also makes posters by hand with metal and wood type, paint and brushes, a habit he picked up from Peter Bankov. This spring he had a solo show, Typoposterized, at PANDA Platforma in Berlin, with a screen printed poster that tries to fit in as many ways of handling type as possible.

items.title: Thiago Lacaz
items.note: Rio designer who makes posters for Brazilian musicians, films and festivals, plus book covers. His animated poster for a micro bookstore's 11th birthday, with coloured bars that read as both book spines and a sound equalizer, was picked for the Typographic Arts 100 this year. His newest posters, for Amaro Freitas and Romulo Fróes, are on Typographic Posters, and he has won first place at the International Poster Biennial in Mexico.

items.title: H.D. Jean, 12oz Denim Indigo
items.note: Needles' exaggerated wide fit applied to a 5-pocket jean in 12oz denim. It has a worn-in vintage wash, darts and an adjustable waist cinch so you can pull the shape in.

items.title: Railroad Pant, Melange Double Cloth Brown
items.note: A roomy trouser based on old workwear, cut from a textured melange double cloth. Haven says it feels substantial but easy to wear every day.

items.title: Field Jacket, Cotton Ripstop Woodland
items.note: A military field jacket in woodland camo cotton ripstop. It has big gusseted chest pockets with flaps and adjustable cuffs, and the fabric is light enough to layer.

items.title: Between Snap Shirt, Poly Fleece Brown
items.note: A loose, unlined fleece shirt with a four-snap front and piped cuffs and hem. It works on its own or as a warm middle layer.

items.title: Watch Cap, Shetland Wool Umber
items.note: A ribbed beanie in Shetland wool, made in Japan. The only branding is a small purple butterfly embroidered on it.

items.title: W/N Wide Pants PT08263OS, Dark Brown
items.note: Wide trousers in a wool and nylon mix, made in Japan. The shop describes a lot of volume through the whole leg and a relaxed drape.

items.title: Wool Mixed Deep Tuck Pants PT07263OS, Black
items.note: Deep tucks give these extra room through the upper leg while the line stays clean. Cotton, wool and polyester, made in Japan.

items.title: Shoulder Stole GD04263OS, Melange Navy
items.note: A generous one-size stole in soft 100% wool, made in Japan. A simple way to add some texture to a plain outfit.

items.title: 101 Dad's Fit Denim Pant, Black Denim Stone
items.note: orSlow's relaxed Dad's Fit jean in soft stonewashed black denim, made in Japan. The shop notes the brand was started in 2005 by Ichiro Nakatsu, who studies old military and workwear.

items.title: Wave Cotton 85-252-006, Black
items.note: A loose long-sleeve crew in a wave-knit cotton with a bit of relief to the surface. It has dropped shoulders and is made in Japan by a knitwear company that runs much of its own production.

items.title: Balloon Wide Pants, Ash Grey
items.note: One of a run of new Beams trousers at Goodhood, in a soft ash grey. It sits alongside wide chinos, wide slacks and wide denim from the same drop, all well under £200.

items.title: Wide Denim Pants, Nep Indigo
items.note: Wide-leg Beams jeans in a nepped indigo denim, new at Goodhood this week. There is also a lighter Dusty Indigo version at the same price.

items.title: 3G Kasuri Nep Crew Neck Sweater, Olive
items.note: A chunky 3-gauge crew neck in a kasuri nep knit, new from Beams at Goodhood. Beams started in Harajuku in 1976, and this is one of the cheaper knits in the drop.

items.title: FISHERMAN-III Mock Neck, Terra Magma Brown
items.note: A fisherman-style mock neck knit from S.N.S. Herning, new in at Kyoto. It is the more affordable of the two Herning knits in this drop.

items.title: LOOSE 720, Dark Blue Vintage
items.note: The loose cut of jeans from Sunflower, a Copenhagen menswear label, in a dark vintage wash. Kyoto also has the slimmer Standard cut in the same wash.

items.title: 11oz Blue Denim Work Coat
items.note: A work coat in 11oz blue denim from Sugar Cane, new at Blue in Green. The SoHo shop is known for Japanese selvedge denim, and this arrived next to new Buzz Rickson's and orSlow pieces.

items.title: Original Spec. Chinos, Olive
items.note: Plain olive chinos from Buzz Rickson's, new at Blue in Green. The same drop has a pea coat and camo combat trousers, and at $170 these are the cheapest way in.

items.title: Vaquero Chambray Western Shirt, White
items.note: A western shirt in white chambray from Jelado, a Tokyo brand with a flagship in Ebisu. It is one of the newest things at Clutch Cafe, and there is a faded indigo denim version too.

items.title: Clutch Magazine Vol. 105: Made in Japan
items.note: The new issue of Clutch, the Tokyo men's style magazine, themed around things made in Japan. The London shop that sells it was set up by the magazine's editor, Atsushi Matsushima.

items.title: Sillage
items.note: A Tokyo label started by Nicolas Yuthanan Chalmeau, made in Japan. Its Circular Pants are very wide and come in one size, with an elastic drawstring waist. Blue in Green and Rendez-Vous both stock it now.
